newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks seen on shaky ground.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen on shaky ground.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks enter the week on slippery ground after posting their biggest weekly decline in 10 months last week, analysts said.
The 476.85 point drop in the Hang Seng index pointed to more weakness ahead, with fears of Wall Street volatility providing an excuse for the market to consolidate further, they said.
"Market sentiment is still very bearish in the short term and buying interest is still very weak," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities.
"It's mainly due to concern about stability on Wall Street and also concern about the interest rate trend in the short term. I think the market will continue to consolidate next week," he said.
The Hang Seng Index fell 3.44 percent over the course of last week, after tumbling 230.78 points, or 1.70 percent, on Friday to 13,379.55.
The drop, the biggest point and percentage decline since March 1996, was prompted by a fall in the Dow industrials, which investors will continue to watch closely, analysts said.

"You just cannot look at fundamentals. You have to look at market trends of other markets and one of the most influential markets is Wall Street," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research.
"If the Dow drops it will have a downward effect on other markets," he added.
Futures trading was also expected to continue dominating the market ahead of the expiration of January futures on Thursday.

Kwong said although weakness seemed to be overdone, a further consolidation period would be healthy after the Hang Seng's recent attempt to move above 14,000 points. The blue-chip index hit an all-time intra-day high of 14,004.93 on January 16.
"I don't think there is any substantial change in fundamentals but there is technical selling because the market tried several times to breach 14,000 and failed," he said.
He said the Hang Seng Index could fall to 13,200 points next week, with the upside limited at 13,700.
Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities, said a deeper slide was possible.

"Investors have seen the market come down for a week and they are staying on the sidelines. I expect there still to be some selling pressure but there should be some support at 13,000 points," he said.
"If they see momentum return then they will come back," he added.

Shares in GZI Transport Ltd are due to begin trading on Thursday. The infrastructure spinoff of Guangzhou Investment Co Ltd offered 250 million shares at HK$3.23 per share, of which 187.5 million shares were offered to international investors and 62.5 million in a Hong Kong offering.

Of the total offered in Hong Kong, 31.25 million shares were available for public subscription, 25 million shares were offered to existing shareholders of Guangzhou Investment and 6.25 million shares were offered to employees.
The subscription period for the Hong Kong public offering closed last Friday and market sources expected a subscription rate of about 300 times.
